correctness.rationale: The exact Chan–Zudilin AZ binomial expansion is checked against original definitions and has term valuation \(3s_2(k)\). Only \(k=0\) and powers of two remain mod16; Lucas converts each to a binary digit. Independent valuation filtering of the Apéry sum gives the previously known \(1+4\beta(n)\) formula. The derived Boolean identity \(2H(n)\equiv n+\beta(n)\pmod4\) proves \(B(n)-A(n)\equiv8n\pmod{16}\), including n=0. The arbitrary-period contradiction uses separated binary blocks at an even multiple of a proposed period. The standalone code checks exact integer sums for \(0\le n\le256\), the Boolean identity on 100000 indices, and 512 period witnesses; no finite check substitutes for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison identifies Chan–Zudilin Cor. 4.3 and Thm. 2.2 as exact binomial/transformation premises, Sun (2013) as reproduction of the same AZ binomial identity, Rowland–Yassawi Thms. 3.28–3.29 as prior Apéry mod16 and nonperiodicity, and Malik–Straub Thm. 5.3 as prior AZ mod8. The explicit coefficientwise same-index bridge \(B(n)-A(n)\equiv8n\pmod{16}\) and the AZ binary formula are not present in the inspected theorems and are not obtained from mod8 information alone. Actual semantic record searches yield no equivalent, although incomplete historical priority is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete all-index exact residue formula for a classical Apéry-like sequence at the first 2-power modulus where the known mod8 periodicity breaks, and links it to a different distinguished sequence by the unexpectedly sparse correction 8n. It is a nontrivial natural infinite-family congruence, carries a sharp periodicity transition, and provides an efficient digital evaluation rule; neither an isolated arbitrary invariant nor a numerical table.
